specs.anchorText: which explains, in one line, why low-light images are grainy
specs.prompt: Simple, cartoon-like educational illustration with clean lines and a warm soft color palette on a clean white background, generous margins: two side-by-side scenes of small buckets arranged in a neat grid catching falling raindrops. On the left, only a light drizzle falls, so the buckets hold wildly uneven amounts and the grid looks blotchy and grainy. On the right, a heavy steady rain fills every bucket to nearly the same level, so the grid looks smooth and even. A friendly cartoon water droplet character watches with curiosity. The metaphor maps raindrops to photons and buckets to pixels. Gentle, approachable, XKCD-inspired, one clear comparison. No text or lettering in the image. Suitable for a technical textbook.
specs.alt: Two grids of small buckets catching rain: under a light drizzle the buckets hold wildly uneven amounts and look grainy, while under heavy steady rain they fill evenly and look smooth, illustrating how few photons per pixel produce noisy low-light images and many photons produce clean ones.
specs.caption: Graininess lives in the light itself, not the electronics: too few photons per pixel and the random arrivals never average out, which is why low light is always noisy.

specs.anchorText: The defining property of aliasing is that it manufactures plausible-looking false structure
specs.prompt: Simple, cartoon-like educational illustration with clean lines and a warm soft color palette on a clean white background, generous margins: a fast-spinning spoked wagon wheel that, when seen through a cartoon camera shutter snapping snapshots, appears to be calmly turning backwards. A small friendly camera character looks confused, and a sneaky cartoon spoke pattern wears a little disguise mask, pretending to be a slow gentle ripple it is not. The scene gently shows high-speed detail masquerading as a false, plausible-looking slow pattern. Whimsical, expressive, XKCD-inspired, one clear visual metaphor, minimal clutter. No text or lettering in the image. Suitable for a technical textbook.
specs.alt: A fast-spinning spoked wagon wheel viewed through a snapping camera shutter appears to rotate slowly backwards, while a sneaky spoke pattern wears a disguise mask, illustrating how aliasing makes undersampled high-frequency detail masquerade as a false low-frequency pattern that was never in the scene.
specs.caption: Undersample fast detail and it does not vanish politely; it puts on a disguise and masquerades as a slow pattern that was never there, which is exactly what makes aliasing dangerous.

specs.anchorText: Blur, banding, clipping: three symptoms, three budgets, one for each.
specs.prompt: Simple, cartoon-like educational illustration with clean lines and a warm soft color palette on a clean white background, generous margins: three friendly cartoon piggy banks or labeled jars standing in a row, each a different gentle color. The first jar holds many tiny dots (samples), and if it runs low its little picture goes soft and blurry. The second jar holds a short stack of flat steps or coins (brightness levels), and if it runs low its picture breaks into visible stripes. The third jar holds a tall ladder spanning a dark cellar up to a bright sun (brightness span), and if it runs short the top of the picture burns to pure white. A small friendly character ponders which jar is empty. Three clearly distinct, complementary ideas, gentle and approachable, XKCD meets Kurzgesagt. No text or lettering in the image. Suitable for a technical textbook.
specs.alt: Three cartoon jars side by side representing the three image budgets: one holds tiny dots for pixels and fails as blur, one holds a short stack of steps for brightness levels and fails as banding stripes, and one holds a tall ladder spanning dark to bright for dynamic range and fails as a clipped white highlight.
specs.caption: An image has three separate budgets that get confused for one another, and topping up the wrong jar buys nothing: pixels fail as blur, levels as banding, span as clipped highlights.

specs.anchorText: Learn what each space is for and the bugs become design choices.
specs.prompt: Simple, cartoon-like educational illustration with clean lines and a warm soft color palette on a clean white background, generous margins: a friendly cutaway of a small four-room house, where the same single cheerful colored ball sits in each room but is described differently in each. One room is a workshop with three paint tubes and a glowing screen (RGB, for devices). One is an artist studio with a round color wheel and a vividness dial (HSV, for picking colors). One is a measuring lab with a ruler and calipers comparing two nearly identical swatches (Lab, for perceptual distance). One is a packing room compressing the ball into a tidy small parcel (YCbCr, for compression). A small friendly guide gestures across the rooms. The metaphor maps one color seen through four coordinate systems, each suited to a different job. Gentle, tidy, one clear scene per room, XKCD-inspired. No text or lettering in the image. Suitable for a technical textbook.
specs.alt: A cutaway cartoon house with four rooms, the same colored ball in each: a workshop with paint tubes and a screen for RGB on devices, an artist studio with a color wheel for HSV selection, a measuring lab with calipers comparing swatches for Lab perceptual distance, and a packing room compressing the ball for YCbCr storage.
specs.caption: One color, four coordinate systems, each built for a different job: RGB for devices, HSV for picking, Lab for measuring perceived difference, and YCbCr for packing bytes.

specs.anchorText: JPEG earns its 10:1 to 20:1 compression by spending the chapter's entire toolkit against human perception.
specs.prompt: Simple, cartoon-like educational illustration with clean lines and a warm soft color palette on a clean white background, generous margins: a friendly cartoon sorting robot standing over an 8 by 8 grid of little detail tiles, cheerfully tossing the fine high-frequency squiggly tiles into a recycling bin while carefully keeping the big smooth low-frequency tiles. Behind it, a photo of a face looks fine to a smiling human visitor but a small worried measuring-tool character notices the missing fine texture and a faint blocky seam. The metaphor maps JPEG quantization to a sorter discarding detail humans will not miss but machines will. Gentle, expressive, XKCD-inspired, one clear scene, minimal clutter. No text or lettering in the image. Suitable for a technical textbook.
specs.alt: A cartoon sorting robot over an 8 by 8 grid of detail tiles tosses fine high-frequency tiles into a recycling bin while keeping smooth low-frequency ones, as a human happily accepts the result but a small measuring-tool character notices missing texture and a faint blocky seam, illustrating JPEG quantization discarding detail.
specs.caption: JPEG keeps the detail a 1991 human eye cares about and bins the rest, but your labels, measurements, and networks are not that human and quietly miss exactly what got thrown away.
